ig_caption:
Free material in the opening is sometimes bait. Here are three classic traps where taking is the mistake.

Noah's Ark Trap: in the Ruy Lopez, 8.Qxd4?? grabs a pawn, then ...c5 and ...c4 shut White's bishop in on b3.
Mortimer Trap: 5.Nxe5? takes a loose pawn, but 5...c6! kicks the bishop and 6...Qa5+ checks the king and hits the knight.
Kieninger Trap: in the Budapest Gambit, 8.axb4?? takes a whole bishop and 8...Nd3 is checkmate, because the e2 pawn is pinned.

The habit that stops all three: before you grab, ask why it was left there.

Slide 4: Kieninger Trap diagram. After 8.axb4, the knight on d3 gives checkmate; the e2 pawn is pinned by Black's queen.

slides.title: Noah's Ark Trap
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6 d4 b5 Bb3 Nxd4 Nxd4 exd4 Qxd4 c5 Qd5 Be6 Qc6+ Bd7 Qd5 c4
slides.take: In the Ruy Lopez, 8.Qxd4?? grabs a pawn. Black chases the queen with ...c5 and ...Be6, then plays ...c4.
slides.edge: The bishop on b3 has no way out and is lost. Safer is 8.Bd5, or 8.c3, giving the pawn back.

slides.title: Mortimer Trap
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 Ne7 Nxe5 c6 Ba4 Qa5+
slides.take: 4...Ne7 looks clumsy and leaves the e5 pawn loose. 5.Nxe5? takes it, and 5...c6! kicks the bishop.
slides.edge: When the bishop moves, 6...Qa5+ checks the king and attacks the knight at the same time. White loses a piece.
slides.movesText: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.d3 Ne7 5.Nxe5? c6! 6.Ba4 Qa5+

slides.title: Kieninger Trap
slides.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Bf4 Nc6 Nf3 Bb4+ Nbd2 Qe7 a3 Ngxe5 axb4 Nd3#
slides.take: In the Budapest Gambit, 8.axb4?? grabs a whole bishop. 8...Nd3 is checkmate.
slides.edge: The e2 pawn can't take the knight: it is pinned to its king by Black's queen on e7.

slides.title: Before you grab, ask why
slides.body: Free material in the opening is sometimes bait. Before you take, ask why it was left there, and look at every check and capture your opponent gets next.
slides.note: Ten seconds of checking costs less than a lost piece.
